findings.evidence: Line 93: `∃ R > 0, ∃ L_R L_L : ℂ, L_R ≠ 0 ∧ L_L ≠ 0 ∧ ...`; line 63-65 of the private `exists_one_sided_tangents` already yields `Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L_R) ∧ Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L_L)`.
findings.fix: Add the two tangent characterizations to the conclusion: `Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L_R) ∧ Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L_L)`. The proof already obtains both from `exists_one_sided_tangents` (line 101, binders `h_tend_R`, `h_tend_L`) and discards them. Otherwise drop the imaginary-part claim from the docstring and module index.
findings.issue: `exists_radius_perWindow_tendsto_log_norm_add_arg` is exposed "for callers ... that need the limit's real or imaginary part" (module doc, line 37-40), but the imaginary part is `((-L_L)/(γ (t₀-ρ) - s)).arg + ((γ (t₀+ρ) - s)/L_R).arg` where `L_R`, `L_L` are existentially bound with only `≠ 0` recorded. Nothing pins them to the one-sided tangents, so no caller can extract any determinate imaginary part; the sole in-repo consumer (OnCurve.lean:349, `Ψ`-argument) uses only the real part. The advertised half of the interface is vacuous.

summary: The rename and deletions are clean, but the newly public `exists_radius_perWindow_tendsto_log_norm_add_arg` exposes an "explicit" limit whose imaginary part is expressed through existentially bound, uncharacterized constants, so the value it advertises is unusable; `piecewise_gluing_induction` is exposed with no consumer outside its own file; and the `C^{1,1}` crossing hypothesis is an 8-binder anonymous existential duplicated verbatim across three public signatures.
